newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $15 to $20 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $15 to $20 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $15 to $20 per tonne higher on Wednesday, in line with gains in London overnight, traders said.

London cocoa futures rose sharply early Wednesday, as the market bounced back from a sell-off earlier in the week. At the midday break, benchmark September was up 17 stg, to 992 stg, the session high.

Tuesday, New York cocoa futures ended weaker, but off session lows. September eased $2 per tonne, to $1,502, after ranging from $1,507 to $1,485. Second-month December fell $3, to $1,549, while the back months finished $5 lower.
Technically, dealers said September was likely to run into some support at $1,485, with the next level at $1,475. Resistance was seen at $1,510, followed by a chart gap from $1,521 to $1,525.
On the fundamental side, Ivorian crop analysts said the country's dry season in July favored drying of mid-crop cocoa (May-Sept) but will not damage pod growth for 1997/98 (Oct-April).
